source: KICD English Language, First Published 2017; Revised 2024 (text layer)
status: outcomes from KICD's text, word for word; skills, prerequisites and misconceptions not yet mapped

sub_strands.sub_strand: Listening Comprehension (Theme 1: Child rights and responsibilities)
learning_experiences: listen to an oral narrative in pairs or groups,
identify words and phrases containing the sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː / from a print or audio text,
say words and phrases related to the theme accurately,
construct sentences using words and phrases with peers.
say tongue twisters containing the selected sounds collaboratively with peers,
write sentences and phrases containing the selected sounds and words,
make an audio recording of a poem containing the sounds /ʌ/ and /ɑː /,
play the audio recording and obtain feedback.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should we say the sounds in words, phrases, and sentences correctly?
How can we improve our pronunciation?
Why should we listen attentively?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration is developed as the learner works with peers to construct sentences.
Digital Literacy is enhanced when the learner uses electronic devices to listen and record themselves.
Learning to Learn is instilled as the learner adopts the use of correct pronunciation in various contexts for effective communication.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility is inculcated as the learner learns about child rights and responsibilities, and practises them while making an audio recording of a poem containing the target sounds and playing the audio for effective feedback.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills: Effective communication is achieved as the learner articulates the target sounds clearly and also listen to audio of the target sound.
sub_strands.links: The learner can link the content of child rights when they learn about child rights and responsibilities in Social Studies.

outcomes.text: recognise sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː /, words, and phrases correctly
use words and phrases related to the theme in sentences correctly
listen for the main idea and specific details for effective communication
respond to information from an oral text
adopt attentive listening for effective communication

sub_strands.sub_strand: Extensive Reading (Theme 1: Child rights and responsibilities)
learning_experiences: select appropriate print and non-print reference materials (dictionaries, junior encyclopaedias, and, subject-specific encyclopaedias),
read selected reference materials independently,
look for information related to the theme from reference materials,
report and discuss what they have read with peers,
visit a library to find reference materials for information related to the theme.
key_inquiry_questions: Why do you read books?
Which type of books do you enjoy reading?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy is developed as the learner manipulates electronic reference materials for information.
Learning to Learn is nurtured when the learner uses reference materials to get information and furthers their learning process.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility is developed as the learner does the assigned duty of selecting reading materials and reading independently.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education: Interpersonal relationship is intensified when the learner learns about child rights and responsibilities and take upon their individual responsibilities both in school and at home.
sub_strands.links: The learner uses the skill on how to use reference materials in all the other learning areas as they all require searching for information.

outcomes.text: select relevant reference materials: dictionaries, junior encyclopaedias, and, subject-specific encyclopaedias on a variety of subjects
spell words correctly for effective communication
use reference materials to find the required information
adopt the use of reference materials for lifelong learning

sub_strands.sub_strand: Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners (Theme 1: Child rights and responsibilities)
learning_experiences: identify demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those, from a text s,
read sentences containing demonstrative determiners in print or electronic materials,
construct sentences using demonstrative determiners with peers,
make sentences containing demonstrative determiners from a substitution table,
use demonstrative determiners to fill gaps in sentences,
search for more examples of sentences containing demonstrative determiners in print and digital texts.
key_inquiry_questions: How do you identify objects that are near or far?
How do we show that objects being referred to are singular or more?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy is enhanced as the learner uses demonstrative determiners in sentences correctly.
Communication and Collaboration is achieved as the learner works with peers in constructing sentences using demonstrative determiners.
Digital Literacy is developed as the learner manipulates digital devices while searching for examples and usage of demonstrative determiners.
sub_strands.values: Respect is developed as the learner respects the opinion of others during activities involving peer engagement such as constructing sentences using demonstrative determiners.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education: self-esteem in the learner is boosted as they learn how to communicate effectively using demonstrative with peers.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies the knowledge gained in learning demonstrative determiners in learning Kiswahili and Indigenous Languages.

outcomes.text: identify demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those, in a variety of texts
use demonstrative determiners: this, these, that, those correctly
promote the use of the correct demonstrative determiner to use during communication

sub_strands.sub_strand: Functional Writing: Filling Forms (Theme 1: Child rights and responsibilities)
learning_experiences: search for sample forms from the internet, individually,
select the information to be filled in a form collaboratively,
fill a form related to the theme using the following details: personal information, school information, parents’ /guardians’ details, religion/county information, favourite sport, hobby among others,
discuss the importance of filling forms correctly with peers,
design a form to obtain information with peers and upload it online.
key_inquiry_questions: Why do we fill forms?
Why is it important to fill forms accurately?
What details do we fill in forms?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy is developed as the learner manipulates digital devices to upload forms on the internet.
Creativity and imagination is enhanced as the learner embraces ideas that inspire creativity when designing forms.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility is fostered as the learner diligently designs a form based on the theme with peers.
sub_strands.pcis:
Life Skills Education- effective communication skills are developed as the learner discusses the importance of filling forms correctly with peers.
Social cohesion is enhanced as learners work jointly to accomplish tasks.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies the content related to child rights and responsibilities which they learnt in Social Studies.

outcomes.text: record specific details: personal information, school information, parents’ /guardians’ details, religion/county information, favourite sport, hobby among others in a variety of forms
design a form to obtain the required information
acknowledge the importance of filling forms correctly

sub_strands.sub_strand: Pronunciation and Vocabulary (Theme 2: National celebrations)
learning_experiences: identify words with these sounds: /p/ /b/ from print materials such as newspapers, magazines,
listen to audio-visual recordings of dialogue containing the sounds /b/ /p/,
visualise saying tongue twisters with the sounds /b/ /p/,
discuss with peers the vocabulary used in the text and construct sentences using the vocabulary,
respond correctly to questions based on the dialogue.
Role plays the events depicted in the dialogue,
interpret gestures, eye contacts, and facial expressions correctly.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should we listen carefully?
Why do we take turns when talking?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy is enhanced as the learner role plays and constructs sentences using learnt vocabulary.
Learning to Learn is advanced as the learner builds on their own learning by taking short notes from the text they have listened to.
Digital Literacy is developed as the learner listen to audio-visual recordings of words containing sounds /b/ and /p/ in real use.
sub_strands.values: Unity is fostered as the learner collaborates with others to engage in role play and answers questions related to the theme.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education: effective communication and self-awareness are enhanced as the learner differentiates the sounds /b/ and /p/ to communicate clearly.
sub_strands.links: The learner can relate the content in pronunciation and effective listening to similar concepts as sounds are learnt in Kiswahili.

outcomes.text: identify words, phrases, and sentences containing the target sounds/p/ /b/ from texts
construct sentences orally using words related to the theme
listen for the main idea and specific details for effective communication
interpret a speaker’s feelings and emotions (non-verbal cues) correctly during an oral presentation
realise the importance of non-verbal cues and appropriate word choice in communication

sub_strands.sub_strand: Intensive Reading (Theme 2: National celebrations)
learning_experiences: make predictions of what a story is about; what happens next in a story using the title/pictures in a story,
infer the meaning of words from the context,
use their imagination to visualise the events in a story,
draw pictures, diagrams, or posters of events in the story,
read poems of not more than five stanzas.,
read a narrative of up to 400 words silently,
retell a narrative or recite a poem and create a video or audio recording of the story.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is the title of a poem or a story important?
How do we predict events in a story or poem?
How do we tell the meaning of unknown words in a story?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and imagination is advanced as the learner participates in activities such as predicting the story by use of pictures and visualising the event in the story as well as drawing pictures and posters on the events in the story.
Learning to Learn is achieved as the learner retells a narrative or recite a poem and create a video of the recording of the story.
sub_strands.values: Patriotism is promoted as the learner shows love for their country when they sing songs or recite poems related to national celebrations.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education: effective communication is enhanced as the learner learns to communicate clearly through pictures or story-telling.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies reading skills in all other areas of learning as they all require reading for comprehension.

outcomes.text: identify characters, places, and events in a story for comprehension
predict events in a text for comprehension
respond correctly to factual and inferential questions for comprehension
use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words for comprehension
recommend appropriate reading techniques to peers

sub_strands.sub_strand: Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns (Theme 2: National celebrations)
learning_experiences: identify reflexive pronouns and collective nouns from print and digital texts,
watch a video clip in which collective nouns and reflexive pronouns (myself, ourselves) have been used in sentences,
team up to pick out collective nouns and reflexive pronouns,
construct sentences using collective nouns and reflexive pronouns,
create and complete crossword puzzles using collective nouns and reflexive pronouns.
key_inquiry_questions: How do you emphasise that you did something on your own?
Which words do you use to refer to a group of things or animals?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Collaboration is enhanced as the learner works with peers to pick out collective nouns and reflexive pronouns from a text.
Digital Literacy is enhanced as the learner watches a video clip featuring nouns and pronouns.
sub_strands.values: Respect is fostered as the learner appreciates others’ opinions when answering questions and creating crossword puzzles collaboratively.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skill (self-awareness) is promoted as the learner learns to communicate effectively using collective nouns and reflexive pronouns in real life.
sub_strands.links: The learner can apply the knowledge gained in learning collective nouns and reflexive pronouns to the same concepts taught in Kiswahili.

outcomes.text: identify collective nouns and reflexive pronouns in texts
use collective nouns and reflexive pronouns in sentences correctly
adopt the use of collective and reflexive pronouns during communication

sub_strands.sub_strand: Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions (Theme 2: National celebrations)
learning_experiences: brainstorm possible points to include in their composition,
write the first paragraph with peers while observing correct punctuation and spelling,
complete the composition of about (100-150 words),
work jointly to proofread their compositions,
display the completed compositions in class,
conduct a gallery walk and give feedback,
search and read compositions online.
key_inquiry_questions: How do we express ideas on different topics?
Why do we share ideas?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to learn is promoted as the learner reflects on their learning as they work collaboratively with peers to proofread compositions.
Critical Thinking and problem solving is advanced as the learner brainstorms on possible points to use when writing compositions and when they complete the composition.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility is enhanced as the learner offers leadership and guidance to others as they collaborate to plan and create compositions.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skill Education is achieved as the learner expresses ideas effectively during discussion and in writing composition.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies the skill of composition writing when learning other subject like Kiswahili.

outcomes.text: select relevant points when planning a composition
write an open-ended composition for comprehension
advocate for the use of creativity in writing

sub_strands.sub_strand: Pronunciation and Vocabulary (Theme 3: Etiquette-table manners)
learning_experiences: listen to correct pronunciation of sounds, phrases, and expressions from the teacher, audio-visual recordings among others,
practise saying the sound /ɔɪ/ in words.
practise using polite words and phrases with peers,
role play the use of polite words, phrases, and expressions during meals,
access correct pronunciation of sounds, words, phrases, and expressions from digital texts,
listen to/recite poems with words featuring the target sounds.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should you use polite expressions when talking to others?
Why should you listen to others attentively?
Which words, phrases, or expressions do we use to show politeness?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-Efficacy is nurtured as the learner engages in role play using polite words, phrases and expressions.
Digital Literacy is achieved as the learner uses digital devices to listen to the pronunciation of target sounds, words and phrases.
sub_strands.values: Love is inculcated as the learner puts the interests of others first through role play as well as listening/reciting poems related to the theme.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education: effective communication is enhanced through the proper articulation of sounds and use of polite expressions.
sub_strands.links: This learner is able to relate the concept on etiquette and table manners to the learning of similar concepts in Agriculture

outcomes.text: identify polite words, phrases, and expressions in oral contexts
construct sentences orally using words related to the theme
listen for specific sounds in words, phrases, and expressions
use polite words, phrases, and expressions to compliment others
recommend appropriate words and phrases for expressing politeness

sub_strands.sub_strand: Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words) (Theme 3: Etiquette-table manners)
learning_experiences: make predictions on a story when reading,
use their imagination to visualise the events in a story,
scan and skim texts for new words and information with peers,
answer factual and inferential questions from the texts,
use digital devices to read online stories for comprehension.
key_inquiry_questions: How do you get information from a text?
Which things do you predict or visualize in a story?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-Efficacy is developed as the learner predicts and visualises stories from texts.
Communication is enhanced as the learner works with peers to scan and skim the text and share information
sub_strands.values: Social justice is promoted as the learner uses their imagination to visualise the events in a story
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education: The learner acquires the skills of living with others from reading texts on etiquette especially table manners.
sub_strands.links: The learner can link the content derived from the theme of etiquette to what is learnt in Agriculture.

outcomes.text: relate events in the story with their life experiences
predict events in a text for comprehension
create mental images from the events in a story
respond to factual and inferential questions correctly
relate events in a reading text to real life experiences

sub_strands.sub_strand: Language Pattern (Theme 3: Etiquette-table manners)
content_topics: Use of Must/Should with an Adverb/ Adverbial
learning_experiences: make sentences with too...to/for from a substitution table. For example, ‘The stone is too heavy for Nanjala to lift.’
construct sentences using: ‘must/should with an adverb/adverbial’ For example, We must brush our teeth every day,
recite poems with the target language pattern.
discuss instances when the sentence patterns are used,
fill in blank spaces in sentences using the patterns,
search for examples of sentences with the language patterns from the internet, newspapers, and magazines among others.
key_inquiry_questions: How do you identify correct sentences?
Why is it important to use sentences correctly?
sub_strands.core_competences: Learning to Learn is enhanced as learners searches for examples of sentences in newspapers, internet, magazines among others.
sub_strands.values: Respect is developed as the learner displays open mindedness and humility when peers make sentences using the given pattern.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education: effective communication is enriched as the learner shows mastery of sentence structures in language.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies the knowledge of the basic sentence structure to learn in all other areas of learning in which English is the language of instruction.

outcomes.text: identify sentences featuring the target language patterns: use of too...to/for and use of Must/Should with an Adverb/Adverbial
use the language patterns in sentences correctly
promote the use sentence patterns correctly for clarity of communication

sub_strands.sub_strand: Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting (Theme 3: Etiquette-table manners)
learning_experiences: copy words, sentences, and paragraphs using joined letters in their books,
observe visuals/pictures and compose a story of about (100-120 words) in cursive script,
discuss the importance of writing legibly and neatly as a class,
team up to search for information from the internet or print sources and make notes.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should we write legibly and neatly?
How can you improve your handwriting?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and imagination is developed as the learner uses visuals to write notes.
Digital Literacy is enhanced as the learner uses internet resources to search for information on visual composition.
sub_strands.values: Respect is fostered as the learner accommodates diverse opinions from peers as they search for material featuring the theme and write compositions based on the characters, places or event.
sub_strands.pcis: Life skills Education - self-esteem and confidence are enhanced as the learner becomes more proficient in self-expression.
sub_strands.links: The learner uses legible handwriting to write texts in all learning areas as legible and neat handwriting is emphasised.

outcomes.text: identify text written in joined letters or cursive script
write legibly using joined letters/cursive script
recommend ways of improving legibility and neatness in written communication

sub_strands.sub_strand: Pronunciation and Vocabulary (Theme 4: Road accidents – prevention)
learning_experiences: recite a poem featuring the words skid, speed, hit and run, reckless, block, traffic, fatal, rescue, ambulance, road signs,
apply the correct stress on the words skid, speed, hit and run, reckless, block, traffic, fatal, rescue, ambulance, road signs,
listen/watch to an audio-visual material on pronunciation,
list the words that are stressed,
practise saying words using the correct stress, with peers for example; conflict (verb)/conflict (noun), subject (verb) /subject (noun)
work jointly to identify the word class of the stressed word,
say words containing the sounds /t/ and /d/,
construct sentences orally using the new vocabulary,
take part in a language game involving word stress.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should we pronounce words correctly?
Why do words have different meanings at times?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner practises correct pronunciation of sounds and words in small groups.
Self-efficacy is developed as learners recite poems and stress words correctly.
sub_strands.values: Peace is fostered as the learner displays tolerance with peers struggling to distinguish between sounds /t/ and /d/ during pronunciation and they as help one another to improve their pronunciation.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety and security is promoted as the learner interacts with content on accident prevention.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies the knowledge derived from the theme accident and road safety to the concept of accidents is learnt in such learning areas as Environmental Studies.

outcomes.text: list words whose meaning differs according to pronunciation (Word Stress (contrast between, nouns/verbs, verb /adjectives)
construct sentences orally using words related to the theme
pronounce words using the correct stress
use vocabulary related to the theme correctly
advocate for the importance of correct use of stress in communication

sub_strands.sub_strand: Intensive Reading: Comprehension (Theme 4: Road accidents – prevention)
learning_experiences: view pictures, illustrations, posters, videos, pictures maps mnemonics, and symbols among others collaboratively with peers,
describe and interpret visuals correctly with peers,
preview and make predictions based on pictures and illustrations related to the theme,
infer the meaning of the words related to the theme,
compose songs, stories, poems or dialogues on road safety and prevention featuring words,
answer questions based on the visuals with peers,
present own stories using pictures or videos,
create visuals based on their experiences.
key_inquiry_questions: Why are pictures important?
How can you use pictures to communicate ?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-Efficacy is developed as the learner reads and interprets visuals.
Digital Literacy is achieved as the learner looks for or watches visuals in digital format.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility is enhanced as the learner composes poems and answers questions related to the theme collaboratively with peers.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education: Effective communication is enhanced as the learner learns how to read and interpret visuals and can therefore communicate effectively using visuals.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies the concept of interpreting visuals to similar concepts learnt in Art and craft. This is also applicable when interpreting maps and charts, a concept taught in Social Studies.

outcomes.text: list the illustrations, posters, videos, pictures maps mnemonics in the classroom
make predictions based on visuals for comprehension
create mental images from text they have viewed, read or heard
answer factual and inferential questions correctly
judge the appropriateness of visuals in conjunction with peers

sub_strands.sub_strand: Word Class: Possessive Pronouns (Theme 4: Road accidents – prevention)
learning_experiences: engage in online/offline games involving pronouns collaboratively with peers,
simulate, dramatise or role play a conversation featuring possessive pronouns,
watch videos/songs involving the use of possessive pronouns,
compose songs based on the use of personal and possessive pronouns,
fill gaps in sentences correctly using possessive pronouns and belong to,
use the words related to the theme in sentences,
create a list of sentences using possessive and personal pronouns and featuring the words,
display the list of sentences on charts and posters.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should we use possessive forms correctly?
Which words show something belongs to a person?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner engages in online games with peers.
Self-efficacy is developed as the learner creates a list of possessive pronouns and displays them in the classroom.
sub_strands.values: Integrity is cultivated as the learner displays honesty while filling the gaps using possessive pronouns individually as assigned.
sub_strands.pcis: Citizenship - social cohesion and integration is cultivated as learners play language games.
sub_strands.links: The learner links the knowledge of pronouns to similar concepts learnt in Kiswahili.

outcomes.text: identify possessive forms in print or digital texts
use possessive forms correctly in sentences
advocate the correct use of possessive forms among peers

sub_strands.sub_strand: Functional Writing: Friendly Letter (Theme 4: Road accidents – prevention)
content_topics: A Reply to a friendly letter
learning_experiences: read a sample friendly letter with peers and pick out the parts such as address, salutation, date, complimentary close among others,
pick words related to the theme such as (pedestrian crossing, risk, slide, smog, brake, emergency, police, license, prevent, safety, vehicle, prevention),
write a reply to a friendly letter using the new words and the correct format,
proofread/edit the letter collaboratively,
present the edited version to other groups,
work jointly to search for more examples of friendly letters on the internet.
key_inquiry_questions: How do you communicat e with people who are far away?
Why do we write letters?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn is enhanced as the learner searches for more examples of friendly letters on the internet.
Creativity and Imagination is promoted as the learner composes friendly letters using the correct format.
sub_strands.values: Love is enhanced as learners reply friendly letters from peers.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education: Effective communication is developed as the learner learns how to write a friendly letter.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies the skills and knowledge derived from letter writing to similar concept learnt in Kiswahili.

outcomes.text: identify the components of a friendly letter from a sample letter
write a friendly letter using the correct format for effective communication
judge the appropriateness of words, phrases and sentences used in friendly letters

sub_strands.sub_strand: Listening Comprehension (Theme 5: Traditional foods)
learning_experiences: listen to a speech and pick out words containing sound /e/,
interpret non-verbal cues such as gestures, facial expressions and eye contact collaboratively with peers,
prepare and make a speech while collaborating with peers,
listen to correct pronunciation of sounds, words and phrases from the teacher or audio-visual recordings,
listen to a poem with various adjectives describing traditional foods,
recite the poem with peers and pick out adjectives,
search for examples of adjectives in the internet, newspapers and magazines.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should we pronounce sounds correctly?
Which words do we use to describe things, people or events?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Citizenship is inculcated as the learner discusses and appreciates traditional foods from different communities.
Self-efficacy is enhanced as the learner’s confidence is enhanced as they recite poems and make speeches while collaborating with peers.
sub_strands.values: Patriotism is developed as the learner shows awareness of own culture and respect for others’ culture as they listen to poems describing traditional foods.
sub_strands.pcis: Cultural awareness: This is promoted as the learner interacts with texts on traditional foods.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies the skill of listening comprehension in all other learning areas as they all require listening skills as a learning prerequisite.

outcomes.text: recognise sounds, words and phrases correctly
listen for the main idea and specific details for effective communication
use adjectives to construct sentences orally
display varied emotions and feelings during an oral presentation

sub_strands.sub_strand: Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials (Theme 5: Traditional foods)
learning_experiences: work jointly to select texts from a collection,
preview a text to determine suitability.
scan a text to pick out vocabulary words,
skim through reading materials for the main idea,
select fiction and non-fiction reading materials of between 1000-1250 words (both print and non-print),
read selected materials independently,
set up an after-school reading club where they meet regularly,
share reflections on the books read collaboratively.
key_inquiry_questions: What materials do you enjoy reading?
Why is it necessary to read many books?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner sets up an after-school reading club where they meet regularly with peers to read.
Digital Literacy is attained as the learner sources for a variety of reading materials online.
Learning to Learn is developed as the learner engages in independent reading which enhances sourcing for information and lifetime learning.
sub_strands.values: Unity is developed as the learner respects self and others’ opinions when selecting and reading fiction and nonfiction materials collaboratively.
sub_strands.pcis: Social justice is enhanced as the learner practises living together through establishment of an after-school reading club.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies extensive reading in other learning areas like Kiswahili which emphasises on the same concept.

outcomes.text: select relevant reading materials from a collection of books
scan a text to obtain specific information
skim through digital or print texts to establish appropriateness and relevance
read a variety of materials for fluency
judge the appropriateness of a reading text on the basis of language and interest

sub_strands.sub_strand: Word Class: Adjectives (Theme 5: Traditional foods)
content_topics: Comparatives and superlative forms of (regular/irregular) adjectives
learning_experiences: describe items using the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives e.g. that window is bigger than this one,
change positive forms of regular and irregular adjectives to their comparative and superlative forms,
pick out adjectives of size, shape and age from a narrative or poem in collaboration with peers,
construct sentences featuring adjectives of size, shape and age,
fill gaps using adjectives in the correct order,
create a crossword puzzle using adjectives.
key_inquiry_questions: How do we compare things, people or events?
Which words are used to describe things or people?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and Imagination is enhanced as the learner creates crossword puzzles and make sentences based on adjectives.
Digital Literacy is achieved as the learner searches for various adjectives on the internet.
sub_strands.values: Peace is enhanced as the learner cooperate with peers to change positive forms of regular and irregular adjectives to superlative forms.
sub_strands.pcis:
Environmental Education is enhanced as the learner is exposed to information on traditional foods.
Hygiene and Nutrition is enhanced as the learner interacts with texts with content on traditional nutritious food.
sub_strands.links: The learner uses this knowledge on comparison of adjectives to learn the similar concepts in Kiswahili.

outcomes.text: identify comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in a text
order adjectives in terms of size, shape and age appropriately
use the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives accurately
advocate the importance of using adjectives correctly in communication

sub_strands.sub_strand: Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions (Theme 5: Traditional foods)
learning_experiences: brainstorm ideas for a narrative composition collaboratively with peers,
read samples of narrative compositions with peers,
identify the parts of a narrative composition,
compose a narrative of 120 -160 words individually or collaboratively,
practise writing own narratives,
listen or view a recording of a narrative and rewrite it in own words,
proofread each other’s work and give feedback.
key_inquiry_questions: Why do you enjoy reading stories?
How do you make your composition interesting?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and Imagination is enhanced as the learner creates and writes stories.
Learning to learn is developed as the learner listens or view a recording of a narrative and re-write it in own words,
sub_strands.values: Patriotism is developed as learners create narrative compositions featuring traditional foods for different communities showing respect for each other.
sub_strands.pcis: Life skills (Assertiveness) is enhanced as the learner masters the art of creative writing and can freely express themselves via writing.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies the knowledge about traditional food crops to other subjects such as Agriculture and Science and Technology which have similar concepts.

outcomes.text: identify the parts of a narrative composition
write coherently on different topics
create a narrative composition for self-expression
promote creativity in writing among peers

sub_strands.sub_strand: Pronunciation and Vocabulary (Theme 6: Jobs and occupations)
learning_experiences: reproduce appropriate patterns of stress and intonation in speech,
sort the statements and questions on the basis of rising or falling intonation collaboratively with peers,
practise saying words, phrases and sentences with the sounds /f/ and /v/,
say tongue twisters with the sounds /f/ and /v/ collaboratively,
watch a video of a dialogue in which statements and questions are used,
recite a choral verse with peers,
use the right intonation on a role play on telephone conversation,
sing songs featuring stress and intonation.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly?
Why do we raise or lower our voices when speaking?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration is achieved as the learner reproduces appropriate patterns of stress and intonation in speech.
Self-Efficacy is nurtured as the learner practises saying words, phrases and sentences with the sounds /f/ and /v/.
sub_strands.values: Respect is developed as the learner displays understanding and appreciation of others’ efforts as they practise saying tongue twisters with the sounds /f/ and /v/.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education: Effective communication is promoted as the learner makes telephone conversations using appropriate stress and intonation for effective communication.
sub_strands.links: The learner can apply the concept of stress and intonation to Kiswahili and other languages that expose learners to stress and intonation.

outcomes.text: sort statements and questions based on rising and falling intonation
pronounce words and phrases with the target sounds /f/ and /v/, correctly
construct sentences orally using words related to the theme
use stress and intonation appropriately in statements and questions
advocate the need for correct stress and intonation in varied contexts

sub_strands.sub_strand: Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues (Theme 6: Jobs and occupations)
learning_experiences: make connections between the characters in the text and the people they know,
relate events in the dialogue to their experiences,
read and role-play a dialogue of about 400 words collaboratively with peers,
pick out main ideas from the dialogue,
answer direct and inferential questions based on the dialogue,
infer the meaning of words from the context (for example, from words occurring before or after).
key_inquiry_questions: How can we guess the meaning of words?
What makes you a good reader?
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication and Collaboration is achieved as the learner engages in role playing dialogues collaboratively with peers.
sub_strands.values: Unity is developed as the learner collaborates with peers to role play dialogues related to the theme.
sub_strands.pcis: Learner Support Programmes - Career guidance is emphasised when the learners read and role play a dialogue on job occupations collaboratively with peers.
sub_strands.links: The learner can apply the skill of reading for comprehension to all other areas of learning as they all require reading.

outcomes.text: select unfamiliar words and phrases from a reading text
use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words from a text
respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension
relate events in the story to their own experience

sub_strands.sub_strand: Word Class: Determiners: Quantifiers: (Theme 6: Jobs and occupations)
learning_experiences: read a passage related to the theme and identify quantifying determiners from the passage collaboratively,
match quantifying determiners with corresponding countable and uncountable nouns,
list quantifying determiners that can be used with both countable and uncountable nouns,
read sentences containing quantifying determiners from the internet with peers,
construct sentences using quantifying determiners with nouns with peers,
complete sentences by filling in gaps using the correct quantifying determiners.
key_inquiry_questions: Which words do we use to show amount or quantity?
Why is it important to tell the quantity of something?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-Efficacy is nurtured as the learner uses quantifying determiners in sentences correctly and learns to apply them in life.
Communication and Collaboration is achieved as the learner reads the sentences with quantifying determiners from the internet with peers.
Digital Literacy is developed as the learner uses the internet to look for sentences with quantifying determiners.
sub_strands.values: Respect is enhanced as the learner accommodates diverse opinions from peers as they complete tasks involving the use of quantifiers.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education: Effective communication is promoted as the learner practises using quantifiers correctly to enable them communicate effectively.
sub_strands.links: The learner uses the knowledge of quantifying determiners to learn similar concepts in language areas such as Kiswahili.

outcomes.text: identify quantifying determiners: few/ a few, little/ a little, a lot of/ lots of, each, all, enough, most, least in a variety of texts
use quantifying determiners few/ a few, little/ a little, a lot of/ lots of, each, all, enough, most, least appropriately in a variety of contexts
judge the appropriateness of quantifying determiners in oral and written texts

sub_strands.sub_strand: Creative Writing: Pictorial Composition (Theme 6: Jobs and occupations)
learning_experiences: interpret pictures collaboratively with peers,
match the pictures with the different parts of a composition: beginning, middle and end,
watch a variety of pictorial compositions collaboratively with peers,
arrange different pictures logically to write a story coherently,
write a pictorial composition of about 120 -160 words,
proof read the pictorial composition,
display their compositions in the classroom.
key_inquiry_questions: Why do we enjoy looking at pictures?
What messages do pictures communicate?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner works with peers to watch a variety of pictorial compositions.
Creativity and Imagination is nurtured as the learner interprets pictures and writes stories.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility is achieved as the learner takes up assigned roles of creating and proofreading pictorial compositions.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skill Education: Effective communication is enhanced as the learner expresses themselves in writing a pictorial composition of about 120 -160 words.
sub_strands.links: The learner can apply the skills to similar concepts in Art and Craft drawing, and Social Studies which features interpretation of maps and charts.

outcomes.text: choose possible topics for pictorial compositions
create a composition based on the visuals or pictures
judge visuals appropriately for creativity in writing

sub_strands.sub_strand: Pronunciation and Vocabulary (Theme 7: Learning through technology)
learning_experiences: select words with the sound: /ə/ and the diphthongs: /ɪə/ and /eɪ/ from a dialogue,
take turns to read a dialogue collaboratively,
interrupt a conversation appropriately,
view a video of conversation and list words or phrases used to interrupt politely,
say the target sounds as modelled from a recording,
make sentences with words containing the sound: /ə/ and the diphthongs: /ɪə/ /eɪ/.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly?
Why should you give others a chance to speak?
How do you tell if someone is happy or sad?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy is nurtured as the learner improves their pronunciation skills by practising pronouncing the target sounds.
Digital Literacy is developed as the learner interacts with digital devices while watching a video.
sub_strands.values: Respect is enhanced as the learner exercises patience as they practise listening interactively, turn taking and correct use of non-verbal cues.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skill Education: effective communication is enhanced as the learner watches a video of conversation and sees how people to interrupt politely in real life conversations.
sub_strands.links: The learner can apply correct pronunciation to learning in Kiswahili.

outcomes.text: identify words, phrases or sentences with the target sound: /ə/ and the diphthongs: /ɪə/ and /eɪ/ from a dialogue
construct sentences orally using words related to the theme
pronounce sounds correctly for accuracy in speech
use words and non-verbal cues to express different moods
challenge others to listen interactively for effective communication

sub_strands.sub_strand: Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non-Fiction Texts (1000- 1250 words) Poems (not more than 5 stanzas) (Theme 7: Learning through technology)
learning_experiences: skim through reading materials to obtain the main idea,
preview texts to determine suitability and relevance,
scan materials for specific details collaboratively,
select appropriate reading materials from a library,
read the selected materials individually,
share reflections on the books read collaboratively,
keep a record of materials read.
key_inquiry_questions: What kind of information do you find in books?
Why is it necessary to read many books?
What do you consider when choosing a material to read?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Collaboration is enhanced as the learner scans materials for specific details collaboratively,
Learning to Learn is developed as the learner selects appropriate reading materials from a library.
sub_strands.values: Unity is enhanced as the learner cooperates and assists one another to select appropriate reading materials.
sub_strands.pcis: Effective Communication is realised in the learner as they read the selected materials individually.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies the skill of extensive reading to select and read non-fiction materials in all the learning areas.

outcomes.text: select relevant reading materials from a collection of books
read a variety of materials for information and pleasure
judge the appropriateness of reading materials on the basis of interest, complexity and subject

sub_strands.sub_strand: Tense: Future Time using will/shall (Theme 7: Learning through technology)
learning_experiences: pick sentences which express future time from a text,
make sentences from a substitution table,
answer questions on future time using will/shall collaboratively,
construct sentences using will/shall collaboratively,
role play activities they plan or wish to do in future with peers,
watch videos offline or online and identify sentences featuring future time with peers,
use computers, tablets or mobile phones to listen to audio materials featuring future time,
make predictions (on events, weather, among others) using will and shall,
create display charts with sentences which feature will and shall.
key_inquiry_questions: Which words do we use to show future time?
How do you tell that something will happen in the future?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner expresses future plans using will and shall in pairs.
Self-efficacy is developed as the learner acquires the skill of making sentences about activities they plan do in future.
sub_strands.values: Social justice is developed as the learner shows democracy when they engage in role play activities to plan or wish for what to do in future.
sub_strands.pcis: Effective Communication is realised as the learner practises basic sentence structures that express the future that they will use in their daily communication.
sub_strands.links: The learner uses the concept of future time in other language areas such as Kiswahili.

outcomes.text: identify words that indicate future time using will and shall in sentences
use will and shall to express future time correctly
collaborate with others to determine the correctness and appropriateness of the tense used in own or provided texts

sub_strands.sub_strand: Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation (Theme 7: Learning through technology)
learning_experiences: read a short text and identify punctuation marks used collaboratively with peers,
use commas to show pauses between words, phrases or clauses,
complete sentences using double quotation marks and commas,
pick out sentences with double quotation marks in newspapers, magazines, articles or internet resources,
play punctuation games with peers,
create posters or charts with sentences with double quotation marks and commas and display them in class.
key_inquiry_questions: Which punctuation marks do you know?
Why do we punctuate sentences?
sub_strands.core_competences: Digital literacy is developed as the learner explores internet resources on the use of the comma and double punctuation marks.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility is enhanced as the learner takes up assigned duties and roles in creating posters with sentences using correct use of punctuation marks.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education: effective communication is enhanced as the learner works collaboratively when picking out magazines, reading and identifying punctuation marks used.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies the concept of correct punctuation in writing in all learning areas particularly in Kiswahili.

outcomes.text: identify commas and double quotation marks in written texts
use the comma and double quotation marks correctly in sentences
advocate the use of correct punctuation in written communication

sub_strands.sub_strand: Pronunciation and Vocabulary (Theme 8: The farm-cash crops)
content_topics: Oral Narrative Featuring Proverbs and Sayings
learning_experiences: listen to a narrative and select proverbs and sayings,
match the vocabulary with their meanings,

practise saying words with the sounds /k/ /g/ with peers,
create tongue twisters with the sounds /k/ /g/ with peers,
search for vocabulary, proverbs and sayings in the internet collaboratively,
listen and view stories of about 130 words and songs featuring proverbs and sayings,
create posters and charts with common proverbs and sayings that the learners can relate to with peers and display them in the classroom.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should we pronounce words correctly?
Which proverbs and sayings do you know?

sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy is developed as the learner searches for proverbs and sayings from the internet.
Learning to Learn is nurtured as the learner appreciate the need to use correct pronunciation in various contexts for effective pronunciation.
sub_strands.values: Unity developed as the learner cooperates with peers to practise using proverbs which encourage cooperation and unity among people.
sub_strands.pcis: Environmental Education is enhanced as the learner is exposed to information about the farm and crops.
sub_strands.links: The learner uses the knowledge gained from the theme to learn some concepts in Social Studies on cash crops.

construct sentences orally using words related to the theme
pronounce words with the target sounds /k/ /g/ correctly
use words, proverbs and sayings appropriately in oral communication
display varied emotions and feelings when listening to an oral presentation

sub_strands.sub_strand: Fluency in Reading (Theme 8: The farm-cash crops)
learning_experiences: scan through paragraphs for unfarmiliar words collaboratively,
search for an article on a topic they enjoy, select a portion to read,
set a goal on the number of words to be read per minute,
find a word or phrase from a word - chart within a stipulated time,
read a text in unison, as a class or small group (choral reading),

participate in a reader’s theatre using a short text from a poem or short play, o select a story or poem that can be divided into parts or characters, o assign a portion to each member with peers, o read a portion of the script orally for practice, o read the assigned parts with peers,
echo or imitate a model intonation and expression as they read a short paragraph or sentence at a time.
key_inquiry_questions: What makes someone a good reader?
How long do you take to read a text?
What can you do to improve your reading speed?
sub_strands.core_competences: Learning to Learn is promoted as the learner practices reading texts at the right speed and pace with the correct expression for effective communication.
sub_strands.values: Unity is enhanced as the learner reads a text and participates in a reader’s theatre collaboratively.
sub_strands.pcis: Environmental Activities are reinforced as the learner interacts with information about cash crops through participating in readers’ theatre.
sub_strands.links: The learner can apply the skill of reading fluency in all other areas of learning.

outcomes.text: identify unfamiliar words in texts for fluency
read a text accurately, with expression and at the right speed for fluency
recommend to peers and parents to read accurately, at the right speed and without hesitation

sub_strands.sub_strand: Sentences (Theme 8: The farm-cash crops)
content_topics: Question Tags on the ‘Verb to be’
learning_experiences: fill in gaps in sentences using double imperatives,

write correct sentences using double imperatives.

Why do we ask questions?
sub_strands.core_competences: Self-efficacy is fostered as the learner formulates school or class rules using double imperatives.
sub_strands.values: Respect is developed as the learner practises using question tags and giving instructions in different contexts.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skill Education: Effective communication is developed as the learner role plays giving and receiving of instructions at home using double imperatives.
sub_strands.links: The learner applies the knowledge of imperatives to the same concept in Kiswahili.

outcomes.text: identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text
use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences
advocate the correct use of double imperatives and question tags in communication

sub_strands.sub_strand: Creative Writing (Theme 8: The farm-cash crops)
learning_experiences: read narratives with formulaic expressions in print and digital format,

key_inquiry_questions: How do we make our compositions interesting?

sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy is enhanced as the learner becomes more proficient in writing creative compositions.
Creativity and imagination is fostered as the learner engages in a dialogue to advance a storyline and composes narratives on various topics related to the theme.
sub_strands.values: Unity is fostered as the learners list similes and proverbs in texts collaboratively.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills Education is developed as writing compositions enhances effective communication skills in the learner.
sub_strands.links: The learner relates this aspect of creative writing to similar skills learnt in Kiswahili.

use similes and proverbs correctly in oral and written texts
create a narrative composition featuring similes and proverbs
advocate the use of similes and proverbs to enhance creativity in writing

sub_strands.sub_strand: Speaking Fluency: pronunciation (Theme 9: Communicable diseases)

respond to oral questions on given texts confidently and with speed,
make one-minute speeches on communicable diseases collaboratively with peers,

Communication is enhanced as the learner makes short speeches about communicable diseases,
Creativity and Imagination is developed as the learner collaboratively makes one-minute speeches on communicable diseases with peers.

sub_strands.pcis:
Effective communication is developed in the learner as they practise delivering the news highlights in the classroom.
Health Related Issues: Communicable diseases- The learner’s knowledge on communicable diseases is advanced as they listen to pieces of news about the same.
sub_strands.links: The learner can link the vocabulary on communicable diseases to their learning of similar concepts in Science and Technology.

construct sentences orally using words related to the theme

display appropriate emotions and feelings when making an oral presentation

sub_strands.sub_strand: Intensive Reading: Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts (about 400 words) (Theme 9: Communicable diseases)

retell the story collaboratively with peers,
use illustrations, the introduction and the title of a text to make predictions,
describe the characters, episodes and places collaboratively in a text,
scan a text for specific details,
answer questions from a text,
state the main ideas from a text,
watch a video related to the theme and pick specific information.

Learning to Learn is enhanced as the learner scans a text for information.
Digital Literacy is enhanced as the learner watches a video related to the theme to pick out specific information.

sub_strands.pcis:
Health Education is enhanced as the learner is exposed to information on communicable diseases.
Environmental Education is developed as the learner reads texts about diseases.
sub_strands.links: The learner can apply the knowledge obtained from reading texts on communicable diseases to other learning areas like Physical and Health Education.

summarise the main points in a text

sub_strands.sub_strand: Word Class: Adverbs (Theme 9: Communicable diseases)

make sentences from a substitution table using the pattern how many...could/would,

construct sentences using adverbs of manner, time place and frequency,

sub_strands.sub_strand: Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks (Theme 9: Communicable diseases)

watch online videos or slides about the correct use of the apostrophe and exclamation mark,

sub_strands.sub_strand: Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Interactive Listening (Theme 10: Leisure time activities)
learning_experiences: listen to a narrative and retell it while expressing different moods or feelings,
construct sentences collaboratively with peers,
say words containing the sounds /s/ and /z/ with peers,
watch a video of a conversational narrative or a choral verse online or offline,
take turns pick out words that show polite interruption in the video,
engage in a dialogue and practise interrupting one another politely.

challenge others to listen interactively during conversations

sub_strands.sub_strand: Intensive Reading (Theme 10: Leisure time activities)
learning_experiences: skim through a text and obtain the main idea,
scan through a text to obtain specific information,

read a text independently and retell it in own words,
answer direct and inferential questions from the text,
watch a video on leisure time and write the main points.

respond to direct and inferential questions from a text correctly

encourage others to pay attention to detail when reading

sub_strands.sub_strand: Word Class: Conjunctions (Theme 10: Leisure time activities)

make sentences from a substitution table using but, or, yet, because, since and also,
construct sentences using conjunctions with peers,
fill in blank spaces using conjunctions in sentences or paragraphs,

sub_strands.sub_strand: Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words) (Theme 10: Leisure time activities)

make sentences to describe how they spent their leisure time collaboratively,
organise the sentences to make a paragraph collaboratively,
write a descriptive composition individually,

sub_strands.sub_strand: Pronunciation and Vocabulary (Theme 11: Sports - appreciating talents)

identify words with the sound /aɪ/ from texts,
practise saying selected tongue twisters collaboratively,
make a three-minute speech with peers,
recite poems with peers,
interpret non-verbal cues correctly.

Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner makes short speeches while collaborating with peers.
